Training manual: maintaining a small community library database

The library stores books, members, loans, and reservations in separate tables. Each book has an identifier, a title, an author, a publication year, and a shelf location. Each member has an identifier, a name, and a contact address. A loan connects a member to a particular copy of a book and records the due date. A reservation records which member is waiting for a book that is currently unavailable.

A librarian must be able to register new members, add books, issue loans, record returns, and find overdue items. Every operation should leave the database in a consistent state. For example, a copy of a book should not be marked both available and currently on loan. Backups should be tested before they are needed. Changes to the database schema should be documented so that another librarian can understand them.

method.workload: Raw text continuation with natural EOS on both backends, no chat template. Predetermined prompts and 128/256-token caps; every run retained.
method.baseline: Merged trained FP32 PyTorch, eval mode, SDPA, KV cache; threads selected only on separate tuning prompts.
method.candidate: The same merged checkpoint exported to F16 GGUF in Ollama/llama.cpp; runtime and storage precision both change.
method.wall: Tokenization + generation + response decoding. Ollama also includes local HTTP/stream parsing. Model loading and explicit cache resets are excluded.
method.ttft: First nonempty decoded content at the local client. PyTorch additionally records its first generated token callback. Ollama chunks may contain more than one token.
method.prefill_decode: PyTorch forward-hook prefill/decode compute durations and Ollama API prompt/eval durations are retained with distinct names; they are not identical timing boundaries.
method.cache: Fresh PyTorch generation cache. Ollama explicitly unloaded and reloaded without a prompt for every measured request; first-call kernel overhead is included.
method.fixed_work_policy: Require both outputs to reach the exact requested token budget, identical prompt token counts, and no reported cached prompt tokens. Retain and enumerate all other pairs separately.
method.quality: Throughput prompts are not scored for usefulness. Prior extraction quality results do not establish long-form quality; raw outputs are saved for inspection.
method.limitations: One machine, four prompt families, short repetitions, no energy telemetry or hardware-level GPU tracing. Memory RSS includes shared pages. No broad quality-equivalence claim.
